plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it guarantees you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you never overpay since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Shading the bid down only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above value risks losing money. With no repeated interaction to exploit collusion or signaling, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no incentive to shade the bid here since payment depends on others' bids, not mine. With a value of $18, I should bid exactly $18.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding below my value only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above risks negative profit. With no information suggesting otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $39, so I will bid exactly that amount.
